checked.label: 71 in 100 (Moore 2003)
checked.notes: Abstract (Europe PMC, 2026-11-08): 82 who reached 2+ weeks off in 'outpatient treatment for marijuana dependence'; 71% lapsed within 6 months, mean 73 days; quote word for word, 22 words. 'dependent' supported ('marijuana-dependent outpatients'). Headline 2 figures, not more hopeful.

checked.label: 72 hours (Scott 2018)
checked.notes: Abstract: 'studies requiring an abstinence period longer than 72 hours (15 studies; n = 928) had an overall effect size (d, -0.08; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.07) that was not significantly different from 0'. Quote uses '...' for the CI, otherwise word for word. Use level: abstract says only 'frequent or heavy cannabis use'; 2152 users mean age 20.6, 68.4% male: basis matches. 'no clear gap' = not significantly different from 0. heavy tag and Counted label fit.

checked.label: Week 1 (Schuster 2018)
checked.notes: Abstract + PMC6587572 full text: 62 abstinence vs 26 monitoring, 55 (88.7%) 30-day abstinent; Table 1 days used of past 90: 57.5 and 54.4 (about 55); recruited from community and a high school in a northwest Boston suburb, July 2015 to Dec 2016; CUDIT at baseline, no diagnosis count; attention improved similarly in both. Quote word for word (with '...').

checked.label: 12 weeks (Hser 2017)
problems: Headline reads as an absolute fall ('grew less anxious and depressed'); the paper compares slopes against the use-increase group, and overall mean slopes did not change (Results 3.2). Caveat says so, but the headline is a bit more hopeful than the source.
'fewer and fewer days' overstates the grouping: people were split only by whether their weekly-use slope went down or up.

fix.numbers[15].headline: In a 12-week weed treatment trial, people whose weed days went down grew less anxious and depressed than those whose went up.

checked.notes: Checked in PMC5607644 full text: 302 with DSM-IV cannabis dependence, 6 sites, Jan 2014 to Apr 2015, 152/150, Table 2 past-30-day use 26.0/6.2, quote word for word (abstract conclusion). Caveat on sleep holds: Table 3 sleep slope -0.06(0.03) not starred in Model I (N=302), -0.07(0.03)* in Model II (N=219). No quality-of-life link. Fix headline is 22 words, 1 figure.

checked.label: I've smoked for years. I'm stuck.
checked.notes: PMC3227547: Table header 'Cannabis Dependence (N=530)', hazard table 'Cannabis remission (N=344)'; 344/530 = 64.9%, 'about 65 in 100' is plain arithmetic. Remission = stopped having any dependence criteria, so 'free of every sign of it' fits. Quote joins two table headers with '…' (word for word). dependent tag right. Test safe.

checked.label: I can't handle quitting
checked.notes: Bonnet 2017 full text: 'The CWS usually lasts up to 3 weeks' (word for word). Connor 2022 full text: 'Sleep disturbances may continue for several weeks or longer.' (word for word). Both describe stopping after long-term regular/heavy use, so 'heavy' is the cautious tag. Proof 1 figure, under 40 words. Test safe.

checked.label: Day 10, I feel fine
checked.notes: Moore 2003 abstract: '71% of those who lapsed, relapsed to heavier use defined as at least 4 days of marijuana use in any 7-day period' (quote word for word, 22 words). 'most' for 71% is fair; '4+ days a week' = 4 days in any 7-day period. Group hooked on weed in treatment: rule 4 met. Test safe (no use drill).

problems: origin is stale: it still says the counterpart was changed to 'Some rough weeks'; the counterpart is now his first two v10 sentences and the third is in notUsed.beliefs[16].

fix.beliefs[3].origin: 06-template.json cannabis belief 2. Limiting kept. Counterpart: his first two sentences kept word for word; the third ('A few rough nights buy my real sleep back', changed to 'Some rough weeks' in round 2) is in notUsed, as no source supports it. checked.notes: Proof checked in PMC5607644: 'A high percentage (68.9%) of the study sample reported poor sleep quality.' (word for word); Table 2 208/302 = 68.9%; sample had DSM-IV cannabis dependence, measured at baseline (still using). 69% is plain rounding. 2 figures. dependent tag right. Test safe for a reader still smoking or already off.

checked.label: Step 1 actions
problems: do[0] holds two ideas (log as usual without cutting down; do the belief tests this week). One idea per line.

plan[0].do: Still smoking? Smoke as usual for a few days while you log; don’t cut down yet.
Do the belief tests above this week too: each one is a one-off trial run.
Already stopped? Don’t start smoking again to do this step: write it from memory.
Allow it. No guilt while you log: you’re investigating, not failing.
Write down what weed does for you: sleep, boredom, anxiety, fun.
Before each smoke, note the time, where you are and what you want from it.
After it, note whether it gave you that, and for how long.
Each thing weed does for you is a belief to test. Start with the beliefs above.

checked.notes: No figures, no source. Safe: no cut-down drill, 'Already stopped?' line keeps a quitter from restarting.

checked.label: Step 2 proof (Ellingstad 2006)
checked.notes: Abstract: 'Long-term daily cannabis abusers (N = 25) who without treatment stopped using cannabis for at least one year'; quote word for word (23 words). 'resolved' fits people who beat a problem on their own. Plain-word paraphrase is faithful; 'A small group.' names the weakness. Outside scope but noted: plan[1].do[5] '80% of the effect is enough' is an unsourced figure.

checked.label: Step 3 actions and proof (Budney 2003)
checked.notes: Abstract: 18 users, 45-day abstinence, 'most effects lasted 4-14 days' (quote word for word). Budney 2004 review (Am J Psychiatry, csam-asam.org PDF) describes this study as '18 daily cannabis users' with no dependence criterion, so 'heavy users, not checked for addiction' holds. Actions: one idea each, safe.

checked.label: Step 5 proof (Gates 2016)
problems: Timing wrong: the source's 'follow-up of longer than four months' is counted from baseline (the same sentence gives '24% at three to four months from baseline'), not from the end of therapy, which ran about 12 weeks. '4+ months after talk therapy' reads as after therapy ended.
'23 in 100 had not used' does not say these were the people given talk therapy (an average across the 8 trials reporting abstinence).

fix.plan[4].proof.text: In therapy trials for a weed problem, 23 in 100 given talk therapy had not used weed in the past month at check-ups over 4 months after starting.

checked.notes: PMC4914383 (Results, point-prevalence abstinence): 'Across the eight studies reporting rates of PPA, an average of 37% intervention participants achieved PPA at end of treatment and this decreased to 24% at three to four months from baseline and to 23% at follow‐up of longer than four months.' Quote word for word, 25 words. treatment tag right.
